review_note: PBS NewsHour reported on September 18, 2003 that the Governor of Delaware had declared a state of emergency for Hurricane Isabel; the exact signing date was not found.

WHYY reported on February 10, 2010 that Governor Markell declared a statewide state of emergency once again, effective at midnight, for the second February 2010 blizzard. The declaration for the first storm (February 5 and 6) was not found.

NOAA Storm Data, February 2003, Delaware winter storm entry for New Castle, Kent, Inland Sussex and the Delaware Beaches, February 16 to 17: 'Governor Ruth Ann Minner declared a state of emergency during the morning of the 16th.' The entry adds: 'The State of Emergency was lifted at 6 a.m. EST on the 18th, except in the city of Wilmington.'

Delaware News, September 8, 2021: 'Governor John Carney on Wednesday formally extended the Public Health Emergency order another 30 days'; 'Under Delaware law, Public Health Emergency declarations must be renewed every 30 days.' Governor Carney had signed the narrower Public Health Emergency order on July 12, 2021, when he lifted the COVID-19 State of Emergency effective July 13 (Delaware News, July 12, 2021). The order was in force when the remnants of Hurricane Ida flooded New Castle County on September 1 to 7, 2021 (DR-4627); no declaration for Ida itself has been found. Per the ruling on this row, it counts for DR-4627, flagged as a lesser declaration and a date-only match for a different hazard.
